spec_issues: The overview and the prompt agree: architecture, tokenizer, mean pooling, cosine ranking and checkpoint initialisation are fixed; training has 900 s and retrieval 600 s; training uses only optifine_public_tests/assets/hotpotqa/train. RETRIEVAL.md adds that '--seed can change between runs'.

The overview says the grader 'reruns the starter's ... training', yet the private baseline is exactly 0.45675789634239594 in all 10 breakdowns, so it is cached or deterministic. This is harmless, and it removes the denominator noise that affects other tasks.

The public panel (queries, corpus and gold for 3,072 questions over 60k paragraphs) ships inside the workspace. The prompt forbids training on it ('Use only the questions and corpus in .../train'), and none of the 12 training.py patches reads it. Panel use was limited to evaluation helpers (Fable aJjZCsq dev/, Kimi 8moZreh dev/).
verifier_issues: The train corpus overlaps the evaluation corpus. 24,389 of the 60,000 public-panel paragraphs, and 2,292 of the 5,922 gold paragraphs (~39%), also appear in the 200k train corpus (Fable 9pA8cjv [15], [87]; Fable aJjZCsq [13]-[14]). Unsupervised pretraining on the train corpus (ICT/crop: Fable, GPT) therefore partly memorises evaluation documents. Fable notes its link pretraining 'only works because ... 39% of gold docs overlap'. The rules allow this, and the private panel is likely built the same way. Even so, the absolute nDCG overstates generalisation to an unseen corpus and favours corpus-pretraining recipes.

The private panel is the same distribution as the public one but a different set. The private baseline is 0.4568 vs 0.4473 public. Every trial's private nDCG lies within -0.001 to +0.016 of its final public nDCG (e.g. Fable 0.7328->0.7394, Argon 0.6627->0.6624, Kimi 0.585->0.6005).

Three trials have no breakdown (both GPT-6 Astra trials and Gemini Flash PhEvjxs). PhEvjxs was scored 0.338 despite an ArtifactCollectionError; that implies nDCG of about 0.611, matching its public 0.6126.
task_level.noise: Run-to-run noise is about +/-0.003 nDCG, roughly +/-0.007 reward (Fable seeds 0.7300-0.7334; Argon repeats 0.6617-0.6630), and the baseline is fixed. Gaps between models are at least 0.03 nDCG: Fable 0.739/0.734 > GPT 0.722/0.708 > Argon 0.662/0.652 > Grok 0.629/0.627 > Kimi 0.617/0.601 > Flash 0.611/0.570. The order is robust, except that Flash PhEvjxs (0.611) slightly overlaps Kimi cMLMUiT (0.601).
task_level.epoch_rationale: The baseline is fixed, noise is far below the gaps between models, the private set is distinct, and no trial broke the data rule. The train/eval corpus overlap inflates absolute scores but does not change the winner (Fable, with both attempts top).
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming was found. Every gain comes from known dense-retrieval techniques: model-mined hard negatives, cross-GPU in-batch negatives, longer schedules, corpus pretraining (ICT/crop), cross-encoder or ensemble distillation, and weight averaging. The main separator is spending most of the 15-minute budget on unsupervised corpus pretraining (Fable ~0.73, GPT ~0.71-0.72 vs ~0.60-0.66 for the others). Fable adds two transferable data-construction ideas, multi-positive composite queries from random paragraph pairs and idf^2 keyword queries, with ablations. Part of the corpus-pretraining benefit comes from the train/eval corpus overlap.

trials.approach: Wall-clock-budgeted two-stage recipe. Stage 1 (~760 s) is ICT-style pseudo-query contrastive pretraining over the 200k train paragraphs: random spans (half cut out of the paragraph), titles, keyword queries sampled by idf^2, and 30% 'two-paragraph' queries that concatenate pieces of two random paragraphs, with both as positives, to mimic two-support questions. Stage 2 (56 s) is supervised fine-tuning with hard negatives re-mined from the full corpus by the current model. Public 0.7328 (seed 1729) / 0.7334 (seed 7); private 0.7394.

trials.approach: Crop pretraining for 85% of the budget on the 200k train paragraphs. 30% of queries are a span pointing to its paragraph; 70% are the title of paragraph A plus a span of an unrelated paragraph B, with both positive. Then supervised fine-tuning with TF-IDF distractors and model-mined hard negatives, run four times and weight-averaged. torch.compile with manual gradient averaging gives more steps. Public 0.7318/0.7300/0.7303 over three seeds; private 0.7344.

trials.approach: A staged recipe with a training-time reparameterised embedding table: IDF-gated deltas, a learned projection and scale (IDFEmbeddingWrapper), exported as a plain BertModel state dict. Mined hard negatives, cross-encoder teachers and distillation, and soups. Public 0.6627; private 0.6624.

trials.approach: Ten training branches with mined negatives and different temperatures and hop weights, averaged into a soup. The concatenated branch embeddings of train queries and documents are then PCA-projected to 128-d and distilled into one BERT-Tiny (a 'procrustes' stage). Public 0.6532; private 0.6518.

trials.approach: Two seeds train in parallel, one per GPU, and are averaged. Stage 1 is in-batch contrastive training with lexical hard negatives and span/title ICT. Stage 2 distils a frozen token-maxsim scorer into the mean-pooled cosine model. Short refinement passes follow (title margins, bridge questions, a topical-word pass). Public about 0.62; private 0.6267.
